title: timed-problem-thread-brynn-owen
content:
Quick gist / raw impression:
- Brynn Owen (backend/infra candidate) — really thoughtful about tradeoffs; comfortable with systems mental model. Answers are measured, leans conservative which is good for runtime infra but might slow decisions in fast-moving GTM contexts.

Timeline of session (my notes / timestamps are approximate):
- 00:00–05:00: intro + resume skim (called out past infra at ScaleMate; built an autoscaler for model shards)
- 05:00–25:00: timed systems design prompt — "design a multi-tenant KV cache for KV-cache+prefix sharing across short-lived LLM instances" (I pushed on isolation/fairness)
- 25:00–40:00: coding sketch (pseudo-Python) for eviction heuristics + bounded async flush to disk
- 40:00–50:00: latency SLOs and failure modes, chaos scenarios
- 50:00–60:00: culture fit + behavioral probes

What stood out (positive):
- Clear decomposition: separated routing, tenant isolation, and cache lifecycle. Brought up vector of QoS (latency tail vs throughput) early which guided rest of convo.
- Good practical heuristics: suggested per-tenant score that mixes recency and request weight to avoid abusing shared cache; proposed greedy compaction windows to reduce memory churn.
- Thoughtful around safety: suggested soft quotas per-tenant + graceful degradation by routing to cheaper model variant — aligns with our fallback patterns.
- Code literacy: wrote clean async sketch that handled cancellation and backpressure; recognized where approximations acceptable.

Concerns / open areas:
- Scaling justification: didn't quantify memory growth or show complexity math for eviction (I asked but the answer was hand-wavy). Need explicit O() for common ops and memory per-entry.
- Multi-region: minimal thought on cross-region consistency — assumed strong consistency which would be expensive; didn't explore weaker consistency models for read-mostly keys.
- Prioritization style: tendency to add safety checks rather than pragmatic short-term wins (we need both). For Dedicated customers, this is fine; for PLG, may delay shipping.

Behavioral signals and culture fit:
- Collaboration: referenced pair-programming incident and how they accepted feedback from a junior engineer — good coaching signal.
- Ownership: anecdote about responsibility for a pager incident; took postmortem ownership.
- Communication: slightly verbose but precise; may need prompts to move from deep dive to 5-minute TL;DR in stakeholder contexts.

Concrete follow-ups I want before feedback loop: (notes to self)
- Ask for explicit amortized cost numbers for eviction algorithm (expected memory per-tenant at 95th percentile, eviction cost per op).
- Send small take-home microtask: implement sketch of the compaction window in repo above (PR link) to evaluate clarity of code and tests.
- Quick async: ask candidate to sketch a cross-region read path with eventual consistency tradeoffs — 10–15 min written answer.

Suggested outcome / next step:
- Recommend: move to one more loop focused on scalability (SRE-ish), give take-home microtask. Candidate looks like strong fit for Senior Backend/Runtime Engineer but we need to validate large-scale tradeoffs and quantification.

Scorecard (rough, on-the-fly):
- System design: 4/5
- Coding & clarity: 4/5
- Production mindset (ops/SLAs): 3.5/5
- Collaboration & org fit: 4/5

Interviewer quotes (verbatim snippets I scribbled):
- "I bias toward predictable failure modes — let’s make failures obvious rather than silent."
- "If the tenant is spiky, you should throttle before the cache dies."

Red flags (if any):
- Slight tendency to over-index on correctness over deployability; check that they can prioritize incremental shipping in a PLG product team.

Action items (for hiring manager / loop coordinator):
- Assign take-home, deadline 72h, reviewer = Amit Rao.
- If take-home looks good, schedule SRE-focused loop (45m), with Leah Kim + one SRE.
- Update JIRA-RT-319 with decision gate and link to candidate artifacts.

Misc / random notes to self:
- Candidate mentioned open-source lib "shardkeeper" — check GitHub contributions to validate depth.
- Could be a good mentor for junior runtime folks — has a patient teaching demeanor.
- Reminder: shorten final feedback text to hiring manager; include exact ask for numbers (95p memory, worst-case eviction time).

Unresolved questions to raise in async score:
- How would they measure success for a tenant isolation change? (metrics, alerting, thresholds)
- Where would they trade latency for cost on a per-tenant basis?

End of notes.

---
Notes to file: informal scratchpad. Will convert to structured debrief once we get take-home result.
